components.label: Step-doubled energy check (X2)
components.plain: An opt-in check of a run's energy ledger, the composite's answer to feature request FR-18, which found that its energy check refused honest worlds at moderate steps while a small misbooking passed it. Each accepted step is taken again as two half steps from the same state: the step's own integration error is then subtracted from the energy residual, and what remains holds any misbooking at its full size. The user adopted it on 19 November 2026 as an opt-in check that registered and judged runs must select, each registration declaring its own cap on the integration error, with no default; with it off, today's check and its programs stay bit for bit the same, and it runs only under the implicit–explicit step ARS(2,2,2), the one scheme its registration tested (D224). It landed on main the same day as FR-18's criterion X2, with the harness that registered and judged the criterion, the check's independent reference, beside it. Its qualification, which D224 set as one run on the boundary worlds against their saved verdicts, gave 13 rows, each with its saved verdict, and FR-3's planted energy error was refused at its step; its evidence on FR-8's worlds stops at a step of 5 ms. It costs about 1.22 times a run without it, compiling apart. Implemented and guarded: a test on main runs it in windows.

components.label: External modules
components.plain: Packages maintained outside Cells could add laws and mechanisms that meet the same checks, accounting and execution contracts as the engine's own. Cells stays under the MIT licence, aiming at broad use (the user's direction, D180, 15 November 2026). Each part would be registered explicitly for one model build, then checked, assembled, compiled and run; registering a module that a model does not use changes nothing. The design note is still marked proposed. On 16 November 2026 the user, asking that others can easily add modules and laws by pull request, confirmed its five open decisions (D185). Contributed modules come first inside Cells, each in its own folder and namespace, under the MIT licence and with a named owner. A conformance kit shipped in Cells checks a module before its pull request; passing it means the kit's checks passed, not that the science is qualified. New physics still goes into the engine's source, as modules of its structure. The example module lives in this repository and is the template contributors copy. Development runs record an outside module's identity, and registered and judged runs also freeze its files. Two additions: the engine will write a declarations manifest, a list of every registered law, operator and kind with what it reads, writes and conserves, so that new modules appear in the documents and in this viewer's laws library without hand edits; and a contributor guide with a pull-request template. The four openings the design asked of the rework landed with it on 16 November 2026: kinds of piece are registered for one model build, exactly as an outside package would register them. Since 17 November 2026 laws and operators register the same way. Its first stage, one law from a separately installed package, is fifth in the plan's order after the landing, with the manifest and the guide. Since 17 November 2026 the import surface a module uses is on main, provisional, with no promise of stability until a first outside module arrives (D195), and the manifest is written (FR-12); since the evening of the same day the surface also exports the declaration types a family of its own needs: the law template, the family operator template and the record of a cited work; the kit, the example module and the guide come with the first stage. Still open: whether the project lists the modules that pass, and automatic checks on GitHub for outside pull requests. On 17 November 2026 the user set its first stage, with one installed external module and the question of a public stability promise, at low priority (D214); the plan keeps it in view as incomplete until its acceptance case passes. On 18 November 2026, with seam F's laws as modules, the surface became lazy: each name resolves on first use, so that a law's module can import it without importing the engine's internals, and a guard holds every module in the laws' folder to importing from Cells only the surface and other laws.

components.label: Source layout by role
components.plain: The user decided on 16 November 2026 (D188) that the engine's source takes the modular layout: each law a module of its own, grouped by mechanism (channels, junctions, pumps, routes, reactions, transport), and folders of their own for kinds, operators, models, numerics, execution, the registry, definitions and records. The older model families move into a folder of legacy code that nothing outside it imports. It is reached by two scripted moves, the older families first, each checked at every commit: the same collected tests, the compiled programs unchanged, all 113 saved worlds the same, and tiers 1 and 2 with no changed outcome. Its first step is done: a read-only tool lists the families from the import graph, and on 16 November 2026 the user settled the list (D189). Nine families stay active, among them four that registered protocols name, whose shared code moves into the modular core; 102 become legacy. Its design note, proposed, and the two scripts that plan, make and check the moves have been on main since 17 November 2026. The note's probe ran the whole cycle on a scratch copy of the tree, never merged: a family moved, a coupled kernel taken out and moved, and every check came out identical. Five refactors came first, on 17 November 2026: the legacy entry point (R1), computed module paths named in full (R2), the parts of seven older modules that active code reaches taken verbatim into the core's folder (R3), and two roots taken from the package instead of from a file's depth (R4, R5). The first move then landed on main the same day: the older families' 334 modules went into src/cells/legacy/ by its committed map, with no hand edits, keeping their sub-packages and their names, with no law, kind, operator or model identifier changed, and every gate held, a continuity resume across the move among them. Move 2, which puts the modular parts into the folders by role, came next, and no checkpoint crosses it (D195). First, as decided on 17 November 2026 (D198), the processes folder is dissolved as the first batch of removals: what an active entry point reaches moves, and the rest retires with its tests. The user decided the same day that the physical laws in it are first carried onto seam F's law template, even those not used yet, each with one reference check against saved outputs of the old code and a visible not-qualified status, after a table that sorts its 33 modules and at a lower priority than the gap-junction work; its numerical methods and geometry machinery wait for the engine's own geometry design, and the batch was held until the user accepted that split (D206). Later that evening the user decided that tested laws of the older code are ported to the active engine, the 54 law IDs behind 38 of the protein atlas's 48 units first, after a read-only inventory and one pilot family, below GARD and the gap-junction work in priority; this amends D196, and the retire batch's two laws join it. Mechanisms already owned are not ported as they stand: calcium handling folds into the cardiac laws, mitochondria into their own design, and the junction flux into FR-16. A law that becomes declared is not thereby qualified (D211). The user then set the chain (D213): the retire batch lands once its gate passes, then move 2, then the core-seams pass. The retire batch landed that evening: 33 source modules that no active entry point reached, 64 validation modules and 951 test IDs retired, and a tag holds every removed path. Its table sorted the 33 modules into 2 laws, 16 methods and 15 machinery modules. The two laws, the held charged-surface work law and conduction (J = σE) on the rectangular grid around cells, are to be rebuilt under D206 and D211, and their reference outputs are saved. Four input kernels that carry BETSE's conventions moved out of the engine, to the BETSE comparison tools. Move 2's prerequisites landed on 18 November 2026. A checkpoint written before a declared source move is refused by both loaders and by the continuity route, and the refusal names the tag where it restores; the made moves are declared in one module of the engine, which this part holds. The one-thread pin for linear algebra has one home, and the planner counts a family as active when the static model table has its row, so GARD's family stays active. For this the lead amended D195 the same day, and the user confirmed the amendment before move 2 landed: the layout a checkpoint was written in is read from its recorded source map, and GARD's frozen lineage reader refuses any changed source without naming the tag, which GARD's documentation names instead. Move 2 landed on 18 November 2026, after the origin-of-life engine's first laws (OL1): 117 modules moved by the committed map, with no hand edits in the move commit, into the laws' seven groups (channels, junctions, mechanics, pumps, reactions, routes and transport) and the folders for kinds, operators, definitions, execution, the registry and records; the processes and core folders dissolved, and no law, kind, operator or model identifier changed. The module above declares the move, with the tag of the tree before it. Its first gate failed, and the record says so: the move's rule for dotted names had rewritten five strings that are recorded data, not live references, and four files built moved paths from separate parts. Each was fixed in a commit of its own, and the landing gate held: tiers 1 and 2 with no changed outcome, all 113 saved worlds, crossrev's 9 of 9, every fingerprint of R1's 274 saved definitions, the pin in all 556 modules, the continuity acceptance test 13 of 13, and GARD's frozen first version and OL1's probes unchanged. No gate covers the BETSE evidence verifiers, the frozen release verifiers, the reports' closeouts or the geometry validation's source maps, and tier 3 is to be frozen again later. The moves are the first step of the order the user set (D194). Files are moved, not rewritten: putting each law's declaration, mathematics and citation in one module is a separate pass. Implemented and guarded: both moves are on main with their gates.

components.label: Run-view output
components.plain: Every run can save what a viewer needs to replay it: geometry, identities, record metadata, events and how each layer is represented (D154). The writer merged into main on the evening of 16 November 2026, with its tests. A run that asks for it writes one view file beside its definition, through the shared output paths, and writing it changes no result. It reads what the tissue model, its kinds and the operators declare of themselves, keeps no table of its own for any model, and writes door S's merged view of each field that operators change; what it cannot state it refuses, or lists as unstated. Its first version covers the composite model and the tissue model alone, and refuses the older families. It also writes the loop block of a living-cell loop (FR-11), with a measure of how well the loop closes. Three format items from the viewer's reader follow; the first, each passive route's kind given as a word and its law's ID under its laws, landed with the core fixes on 18 November 2026, and the rest with the tissue model's guard landing by 19 November 2026: what a route's carried species mean, and when a reference constant is written. components.plain: How a law is declared and found. components.label: Passive routes and their laws
components.plain: The tissue model's passive routes kind and the route laws it hosts. The first is a law for molecules that cross a membrane on their own, down their gradient: the one law added in the rework round, to show that adding a law changes nothing for worlds that do not use it. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026 it is on main as one of the tissue model's passive routes, beside a proton leak that compartment pH uses. For an uncharged molecule its core computation is the membrane transport's own route at zero charge, and it books the heat it releases exactly, as the free energy lost by what it moved. In a closed test with two compartments it must conserve material, stop when both sides are at equal chemical potential, reverse with the driving force, and turn the free energy lost into heat with no work from outside. Its independent reference, written by a separate agent that read no engine code, landed on 15 November 2026: in it, flow and heat are exactly zero at equal concentrations, the flow reverses exactly, and heat never decreases. The engine's operator for secretion and uptake is a driven route that books work, so it does not count as passive. Implemented and guarded: on a closed pair of compartments, a test on main shows it relaxing as the independent closed form says, conserving material, and booking as heat the engine's own decrease of free energy, to rounding. It has not been judged against its own reference, and its composition with water is still a target; the passive routes ran in FR-4's and FR-5's judged acceptances on 17 November 2026, which passed, and their scope line names the compartment operator as built at 32a1d439. On 17 November 2026 the gap-junction work found that its exact heat booking refused a step when a route's share of heat was negative by rounding alone (FR-19). It was fixed that evening: a share is refused only beyond a rounding floor scaled by its own terms, admitted shares are booked as computed, every step admitted before is bitwise unchanged, and the law keeps its identifier (D148). components.label: Test tiers gate
components.plain: The routine gate: every test file's outcome is compared with a recorded baseline before code lands. A file counts as changed when its exit code or its count of failures or errors differs, when its count of passing tests falls, or when its count of skipped tests rises. At D172's landing on 16 November 2026, tiers 1 and 2 (492 files) showed no changed outcome. Of tier 3's 229 files, 187 passed, and each of the other 42 was classified, none of them a defect of the round: 23 failures and 16 time-outs that were there before, two tests the round left stale, fixed in the next commit, and one that passes when run alone. The user's rule of the same day (D187) is to test as little as possible but enough for the science: each claim is proved once, at the cheapest level that can prove it, a new test must catch a planted error, and each landing's tier-3 table is frozen as the record the next run is compared with. The audit's tools merged on the evening of 16 November 2026: tier 3's table is frozen test by test, so that a later run of tier 3 is compared test by test instead of running old code again. The user approved the audit's firm list of tests to retire the same evening (D189), and the retire merged early on 17 November 2026: 11 whole files of tier 3 and 40 of tiers 1 and 2 were deleted, and 811 cases were removed from 42 more, while eight rows were held instead, each with its reason. The tiers now hold 327, 152 and 222 files, and tier 3's frozen record holds 218 files and 6,869 tests. The saving is 5.5 processor-hours per run of tier 3 and 2 minutes per gate of tiers 1 and 2. The tree before the retire is tagged, so that every retired test stays recoverable. On 19 November 2026 the user set the suite's policy on cost (D224): a fix adds a row to an existing parametrized test or nothing, a new test that compiles or runs a world states its seconds and its reason at landing, and tests no longer needed are removed in batches, each with a removal list. Tiers 1 and 2 then held 589 files, 172 processor-minutes in all. The tier record's tools gained a fold and a merge, which put a landing's measured rows onto main's record.
